thread:
Alex Chen: FYI I'm kicking off a small project to build a 'modular iac distribution factory' for partner Terraform modules — goal is a repeatable pipeline that packages variants (marketplace, onprem, govcloud) and an index for customers to consume. Thoughts?
Maria G: love the name. Do we have a list of target partner requirements yet? marketplace metadata, license, scanning, etc.
Chad Patel: requirements we should bake in: semver tagging, signed releases, SBOM, terraform fmt & validate in CI, and an automated smoke deploy to a test project.
Emily R: +1. Also need a compatibility matrix (provider versions, terraform version, arm/x86 images for provider binaries). We had issues earlier with provider pinning on Ampere.
Samir (partner-eng): For partners we should provide two distribution channels: 1) a curated marketplace package (cloud vendor), 2) a raw module bundle they can embed. Each needs slightly different metadata (e.g., marketplace requires thumbnail, partner-id, legal contact).
Alex Chen: good call. Let's sketch the pipeline stages: lint -> unit tests (terratest) -> build bundle -> generate metadata.json -> sign -> publish to staging index -> smoke deploy -> notify partner.
Maria G: Can we include an optional 'reference-arch' artifact with a small example app + infra? Partners appreciate a tiny end-to-end.
Chad Patel: yes, but keep the ref-arch as a separate artifact to avoid large downloads. Maybe a lightweight k8s sample + single VM example.
Emily R: CI hooks: circleci/gh-actions ok? We should standardize on GH actions for partner repos so partners can fork templates easily.
Alex Chen: let's standardize on GH Actions and a reusable workflow action in the redwood org. Action inputs: release-channel, target-cloud, enable-telemetry (bool).
Samir (partner-eng): marketplace constraints: Azure wants ARM template overlay for certain SKUs, AWS marketplace wants AMI mapping + listing pages. We'll need a small adapter generator.
Chad Patel: adapter generator sounds right. Could be a template engine that takes module outputs and emits the vendor-specific packaging. Keep it pluggable.
Maria G: security: add SCA scanning (dependabot/renovate + snyk/ghas) and a gating policy that denies publish if high severity. Also require a signed CLA mention in metadata for partner authors.
Emily R: telemetry: include an opt-in usage ping in the sample app (default off). And provide a privacy + dataflow doc to ship with each ref-arch.
Alex Chen: who can own the reusable GH action and the index service? I'd suggest eng-platform for the action and partnerships to own the metadata schema + partner checklist.
Chad Patel: eng-platform will take the action; I'll slot it on our backlog. We need a simple index API — static JSON backed by S3 + signed manifests should be fine.
Samir (partner-eng): partners want versioned URLs for their bundles for easy pinning. Make sure index entries include digest and multiple artifact URLs (marketplace, raw-bundle, ref-arch).
Maria G: what about rollout & revocation? If a module has a critical vulnerability, we need an emergency de-list flow and fast communication to customers.
Alex Chen: add a 'status' field in metadata (published, deprecated, revoked) and an internal playbook for revocation (unpublish from index, mark status revoked, send partner and customer emails).
Chad Patel: tests: terratest matrix against small infra accounts on AWS/GCP/Azure. We can run smoke tests using smaller instance types and a cost cap to avoid runaway bills.
Emily R: add a step that runs terraform plan and inspects diff for dangerous operations (destroy/replace). If plan includes destroy of non-test-owned resources, fail the job.
Samir (partner-eng): partner docs: supply a /docs/quickstart.md, a marketplace checklist, and a compliance checklist (KMS, logging, data residency options). Partners often miss the KMS bit.
Alex Chen: timeline proposal: week 1: schema + GH action proto. week 2: index prototype + adapter generator. week 3: run 2 partners through staging. Does that sound reasonable?
Maria G: timeline OK, but add one extra sprint for marketplace compliance reviews — they usually take longer.
Chad Patel: cool. I'll create an initial GH repo template: redwood/partner-iac-factory. It will include: workflows/, templates/, scripts/generate-adapter.py, metadata-schema.json.
Emily R: include example terraform module using providers v1.5+ with explicit provider constraints and a CI example.
Samir (partner-eng): I'll prep two partners to try staging next month (one cloud SI and one HW partner). I'll also gather their marketplace metadata requirements.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone. I'll open an RFC doc and a small tracking ticket. Tagging next steps: @Maria G to own partner checklist, @Chad Patel to own GH action + repo template, @Emily R to own test matrix, @Samir (partner-eng) to coordinate partner trials.
deploy-bot: build 2791234567-branch: pipeline succeeded — artifact candidate published to staging-index (s3://redwood-partner-staging/2791234567/module-bundle.tgz) :shipit:
Maria G: awesome, can we add a short README for partners: 'how to plug into GH action' — minimal steps, expected outputs, and metadata example. I can draft it.
Alex Chen: perfect. Draft README + initial metadata-schema.json in the repo and we can iterate. Thanks all.
summary: Coordination thread to design a repeatable pipeline ("modular iac distribution factory") for packaging and publishing partner Terraform modules to marketplace and raw-bundle channels, covering CI/workflows, metadata, signing, adapters for vendor packaging, tests, security gates, and rollout/revocation procedures.
